context.title: Computer Engineering Curricula 2016
context.passage: The scientific method (hypothesis formation, experimentation and data collection, analysis) represents a basis methodology for much of the discipline of computer engineering, and students should have a solid exposure to this methodology. Computer engineering students need knowledge of natural sciences, such as physics and chemistry. Basic physics concepts in electricity and magnetism form the basis for much of the underlying electrical engineering content in the body of knowledge.

context.label: S2
context.title: Curated note: Mathematics for Machine Learning and Data Science Specialization
context.passage: For Computer Engineering students who fear math, the practical message is that math ability can be developed gradually. Students do not need to know every advanced topic before starting programming or introductory AI, but deeper AI and data science work becomes easier when the student strengthens these foundations. Student-facing guidance: review algebra and functions before calculus, learn vectors and matrices for linear algebra, practice probability/statistics with real datasets, and connect math to code through small projects.

context.label: S3
context.title: Math Preparation for the College of Engineering
context.passage: The Physics Barrier The PHYSICS 5 or 7 series (required for all engineering majors) is heavily calculus-based. PHYSICS 5A or 7A: These requirements need you to have already completed or be concurrently enrolled in the second semester of Calculus (MATH 52). This means MATH 51 (Calculus 1) needs to be completed before you even start the Physics series.

context.passage: Page 75 Programming skills are highly versatile and applicable in a wide range of fields. They enhance problem-solving abilities, promote creativity and innovation, and offer numerous career opportunities. context.passage: For Computer Engineering advising, this source helps explain why students should learn software development habits early. Useful habits include reading requirements carefully, designing before coding, using version control, testing and debugging systematically, reviewing code, documenting decisions, thinking about maintainability, and treating security and quality as part of engineering rather than as optional extras. The source also helps distinguish programming from software engineering.
